source_text: δ' ἂν εἴη καὶ τοῦδε Χριστὸς, φωτὸς μὲν ὅτι διέλαμψε δίκην, αὐγαῖς δηλονότι ταῖς νοηταῖς ἀστράπτων ὡς Θεὸς, τοῦ ἀργύρου σημαίνοντος. Ὅτι δὲ λαμπρὸς καὶ εὐηχὴς ὁ περὶ γῆν αὐτῷ πεποίηται λόγος, τοῦτ' ἔστι, τὸ κήρυγμα τὸ εὐαγγελικὸν, τοῦ περιαργύρου χαλκοῦ πλαγίως ἡμῖν ὑπεμφαίνοντος. Εὐηχὴς μὲν γὰρ καὶ ὁ χαλκὸς, λαμπρὸν δὲ δὴ λίαν καὶ διαφανὲς τοῦ ἀργύρου τὸ χρῆμα. Ἔνεστι δὲ τοῦτο τοῖς εὐαγγελικοῖς κηρύγμασι, καὶ κατίδοι τις ἂν, τοῦ Σωτῆρος τὸν λόγον, ἔχοντα μὲν τῆς εἰς ἄκρον εὐσεβείας τὸ διειδές τε καὶ καθαρὸν, ὅλην δὲ ὥσπερ περιβομβοῦντα τὴν οἰκουμένην. Εἰ δὲ δή τις ἕλοιτο τοὺς ἁγίους ἀποστόλους καὶ εὐαγγελιστὰς ὡς ἐν τοῖς τοιοῖσδε τυχὸν ἀνατυποῦσθαι στύλοις, λογιεῖται τὰ εἰκότα. Καὶ γάρ εἰσιν ἀληθῶς ὥσπερ ἠργυρωμένοι, διὰ τὸ ἐν μεθέξει γενέσθαι Χριστοῦ τοῦ φωτίζοντος. Τοιγάρτοι φησί· «Καὶ ἔσται ἡ λαμπρότης Κυρίου τοῦ Θεοῦ ἡμῶν ἐφ' ἡμᾶς.» Ὀνομάζονται δὲ καὶ «Τοῦ κόσμου φῶς,» χαλκῷ δὲ περιαργύρῳ μονονουχὶ καὶ ἐμβεβηκότες. Ἔρεισμα γὰρ αὐτοῖς, ὥσπερ τῷ λαμπρῷ καὶ εὐηχεστάτῳ κεχρῆσθαι λόγῳ. «Κύριος γὰρ,» φησὶ, «δώσει ῥῆμα τοῖς εὐαγγελιζομένοις δυνάμει πολλῇ.» Ὡραῖοι δὲ καὶ οἱ πόδες τῶν εὐαγγελιζομένων τὰ ἀγαθὰ, γέγραπται. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Βαθὺς μὲν ὁ λόγος, πλὴν, ἀληθείας ἐγγύς. {ΚΥΡ.} Συμπεπερασμένων δὴ οὖν καὶ τῶν ἐπὶ ταῖς αὐλαῖς τεθεσπισμένων, εἰς ἐλαίου τε καὶ μύρου καὶ μὴν καὶ θυμιαμάτων μετατρέπει κατασκευὴν, οὕτω λέγων· «Καὶ σὺ, σύνταξον τοῖς υἱοῖς Ἰσραήλ· καὶ λαβέτωσάν σοι ἔλαιον ἐξ ἐλαιῶν ἄτρυγον, καθαρὸν, κεκομμένον εἰς φῶς καῦσαι, ἵνα καίηται λύχνος διαπαντὸς ἐν τῇ σκηνῇ τοῦ μαρτυρίου, ἔξωθεν τοῦ καταπετάσματος τοῦ ἐπὶ τῆς διαθήκης, καὶ καύσει αὐτὸ ὁ Ἀαρὼν καὶ οἱ υἱοὶ αὐτοῦ ἀφ' ἑσπέρας ἕως πρωῒ, ἐναντίον Κυρίου, νόμιμον αἰώνιον εἰς τὰς γενεὰς ὑμῶν, παρὰ τῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραήλ.» {ΠΑΛΛ.} Καὶ τί δὴ τοῦτό ἐστιν; {ΚΥΡ.} Ἀναγκαιοτάτην ἔχει τὴν δήλωσιν, καὶ σοφὸν εἶναί φημι τὸ αἴνιγμα· ἑπτὰ μὲν γὰρ λύχνοις, καιομένοις. τε ἀεὶ καὶ φαίνουσιν ἐν τῇ ἁγίᾳ σκηνῇ, τὸν διὰ Χριστοῦ φωτισμὸν παρεικαστέον εὖ μάλα, διαρκῶς ἔχοντα πρὸς τὸ ἐλλάμπειν δύνασθαι καὶ ἀνακαίειν, ἤτοι ἀναμεστοῦν, τῶν πιστευόντων τὸν νοῦν. Ἀριθμὸς γάρ πως ὁ εἰς ἑπτὰ τὴν τῆς τελειώσεως δήλωσιν ὑπεμφαίνει πανταχῆ. Ὡς ἔν γε τῷ φάναι τυχὸν, «Στεῖρα δὲ ἔτεκεν ἑπτὰ» τοῦτ' ἔστι, πλεῖστά τε καὶ ὅσα ἐχρῆν εἶναι πρὸς αὐτάρκειαν. Ἀνακαίουσι δὲ τοὺς λύχνους Ἀαρών τε καὶ οἱ λοιποὶ, οἱ καὶ μετ' αὐτὸν ἱερεῖς. Ἄσβεστος γὰρ ὥσπερ ὁ παρὰ Χριστοῦ φωτισμὸς ἐν Ἐκκλησίαις σώζεται ταῖς τῶν ἱερᾶσθαι κεκληρωκότων ἐπιεικείαις, οἳ ταῖς εἰς ὀρθότητα μυσταγωγίαις τὸν τῶν πιστευόντων καταλαμπρύνουσι νοῦν. Τουτὶ γὰρ, οἶμαι, ἔστι τὸ ἀνακαίεσθαι τοὺς λύχνους ἀπὸ ἑσπέρας ἕως πρωΐ. Σκοτίαν δὲ οἶμαι τὴν ἐκ διαβόλου πλάνησιν, καὶ νοητὴν ὥσπερ τινὰ νύκτα κατὰ νοῦν ἀνθρώποις συμβαίνουσαν, τὰ τῶν
pass_a_gloss: [cont.] A typos of this too would be Christ: that he dielampse (shone through) like phōs, astraptōn (flashing) as God with noētai (intelligible) augai (rays), the argyros signifying it. That the logos pepoiētai (made) by him peri gēn (around the earth) is lampros (bright) and euēchēs (well-sounding), that is, the kērygma euangelikon, the periargyros chalkos plagiōs hypemphainei (obliquely hints). For chalkos is euēchēs, argyros lampron and diaphanes. This enesti in the gospel preaching: one might see the Saviour's logos having the dieides (clearness) and katharon of eusebeia to the utmost, and peribombounta (resounding around) the whole oikoumenē. If one heloito (chooses) the holy apostoloi and euangelistai anatypousthai (to be figured) in such pillars, logieitai ta eikota (he will reckon reasonably). For they are truly as ērgyrōmenoi (silvered) through methexis (participation) in Christ ho phōtizōn. So it says: 'estai hē lamprotēs of the Lord our God upon us.' They are named 'light of the kosmos', and mononouchi (all but) embebēkotes (standing on) silver-covered bronze; their ereisma (support) is kechrēsthai (to use) the bright and euēchestatos logos. 'For the Lord will give rhēma to those euangelizomenoi with much dynamis.' Hōraioi (beautiful) the podes of those announcing good things, gegraptai. PALL.: bathys the logos, yet alētheias engys. CYR.: the things tethespismena (decreed) about the aulai being sympeperasmena (completed), he metatrepei (turns) to the kataskeuē of elaion, myron and thymiamata: 'You, syntaxon (command) the sons of Israel; let them take for you elaion ex elaiōn atrygon (without lees), katharon, kekommenon (beaten) to burn for light, that a lychnos may burn diapantos (always) in the skēnē tou martyriou, outside the katapetasma over the diathēkē; Aaron and his sons shall burn it from evening to morning before the Lord, nomimon aiōnion for your geneai, from the sons of Israel.' PALL.: what is this? CYR.: it has anankaiotatē dēlōsis, and sophon the ainigma: to seven lychnoi always burning and shining in the holy skēnē pareikasteon (must be compared) the phōtismos through Christ, diarkōs echonta (sufficing) to ellampein and anakaiein (kindle), ētoi anamestoun (or fill), the nous of believers. The arithmos seven hypemphainei teleiōsis everywhere, as in 'steira eteken hepta', that is, very many and as many as needed pros autarkeian. Aaron and the other priests after him anakaiousi the lamps; for asbestos (unquenched) the phōtismos from Christ sōzetai in the Ekklēsiai by the epieikeiai (uprightness) of those keklērōkotes (allotted) to serve as priests, who by mystagōgiai eis orthotēta katalamprynousi (make bright) the nous of believers. This, oimai, is the lighting from evening to morning. skotia, oimai, = the planēsis from the diabolos, a noētē night kata noun befalling men, the [cont. §29: unholy heretics' mytharia].
pass_a_gloss_with_greek: [cont.] A τύπος of this too would be Christ: that he διέλαμψε (shone through) like φῶς, ἀστράπτων (flashing) as God with νοηταί (intelligible) αὐγαί (rays), the ἄργυρος signifying it. That the λόγος πεποίηται (made) by him περὶ γῆν (around the earth) is λαμπρός (bright) and εὐηχής (well-sounding), that is, the κήρυγμα εὐαγγελικόν, the περιάργυρος χαλκός πλαγίως ὑπεμφαίνει (obliquely hints). For χαλκός is εὐηχής, ἄργυρος λαμπρόν and διαφανές. This ἔνεστι in the gospel preaching: one might see the Saviour's λόγος having the διειδές (clearness) and καθαρόν of εὐσέβεια to the utmost, and περιβομβοῦντα (resounding around) the whole οἰκουμένη. If one ἕλοιτο (chooses) the holy ἀπόστολοι and εὐαγγελισταί ἀνατυποῦσθαι (to be figured) in such pillars, λογιεῖται τὰ εἰκότα (he will reckon reasonably). For they are truly as ἠργυρωμένοι (silvered) through μέθεξις (participation) in Christ ὁ φωτίζων. So it says: 'ἔσται ἡ λαμπρότης of the Lord our God upon us.' They are named 'light of the κόσμος', and μονονουχί (all but) ἐμβεβηκότες (standing on) silver-covered bronze; their ἔρεισμα (support) is κεχρῆσθαι (to use) the bright and εὐηχέστατος λόγος. 'For the Lord will give ῥῆμα to those εὐαγγελιζόμενοι with much δύναμις.' Ὡραῖοι (beautiful) the πόδες of those announcing good things, γέγραπται. PALL.: βαθύς the λόγος, yet ἀληθείας ἐγγύς. CYR.: the things τεθεσπισμένα (decreed) about the αὐλαί being συμπεπερασμένα (completed), he μετατρέπει (turns) to the κατασκευή of ἔλαιον, μύρον and θυμιάματα: 'You, σύνταξον (command) the sons of Israel; let them take for you ἔλαιον ἐξ ἐλαιῶν ἄτρυγον (without lees), καθαρόν, κεκομμένον (beaten) to burn for light, that a λύχνος may burn διαπαντός (always) in the σκηνὴ τοῦ μαρτυρίου, outside the καταπέτασμα over the διαθήκη; Aaron and his sons shall burn it from evening to morning before the Lord, νόμιμον αἰώνιον for your γενεαί, from the sons of Israel.' PALL.: what is this? CYR.: it has ἀναγκαιοτάτη δήλωσις, and σοφόν the αἴνιγμα: to seven λύχνοι always burning and shining in the holy σκηνή παρεικαστέον (must be compared) the φωτισμός through Christ, διαρκῶς ἔχοντα (sufficing) to ἐλλάμπειν and ἀνακαίειν (kindle), ἤτοι ἀναμεστοῦν (or fill), the νοῦς of believers. The ἀριθμός seven ὑπεμφαίνει τελείωσις everywhere, as in 'στεῖρα ἔτεκεν ἑπτά', that is, very many and as many as needed πρὸς αὐτάρκειαν. Aaron and the other priests after him ἀνακαίουσι the lamps; for ἄσβεστος (unquenched) the φωτισμός from Christ σώζεται in the Ἐκκλησίαι by the ἐπιείκειαι (uprightness) of those κεκληρωκότες (allotted) to serve as priests, who by μυσταγωγίαι εἰς ὀρθότητα καταλαμπρύνουσι (make bright) the νοῦς of believers. This, οἶμαι, is the lighting from evening to morning. σκοτία, οἶμαι, = the πλάνησις from the διάβολος, a νοητή night κατὰ νοῦν befalling men, the [cont. §29: unholy heretics' μυθάρια].
pass_b_english: Cyril: …of Christ. The silver shows that he shone out like light, flashing as God with rays the mind perceives. And the bronze overlaid with silver hints to us, indirectly, that the word he has spread over the earth, that is, the preaching of the gospel, is bright and resonant. For bronze rings clear, and silver is very bright and gleaming. This is true of the gospel preaching: one can see that the Savior’s word has the clearness and purity of the highest piety, and that it resounds, as it were, through the whole inhabited world. And if anyone prefers to see the holy apostles and evangelists figured in such pillars, his reasoning will be sound. For they are truly silvered, as it were, because they have come to share in Christ, who gives light. That is why it says, ‘And the brightness of the Lord our God shall be upon us’ (Psalm 90:17). They are also called ‘the light of the world’ (Matthew 5:14), and they all but stand on bronze overlaid with silver. For their support is, as it were, the bright and most resonant word they use. ‘For the Lord,’ it says, ‘will give a word to those who preach the good news with great power’ (Psalm 68:11). And it is written, ‘Beautiful too are the feet of those who bring good news of good things’ (Romans 10:15).
Palladius: The explanation is deep, but it comes close to the truth.

Cyril: Now that the commands about the court are complete, he turns to the preparation of oil, perfume and incense, saying: ‘And you, command the sons of Israel, and let them bring you pure oil from olives, free of dregs, beaten, to burn for light, so that a lamp may burn continually in the tent of witness, outside the veil that is over the covenant. And Aaron and his sons shall burn it from evening until morning before the Lord, a perpetual ordinance throughout your generations, from the sons of Israel’ (Exodus 27:20–21).
Palladius: And what does this mean?

Cyril: What it shows is most necessary, and I call the riddle a wise one. With the seven lamps (Exodus 25:37), which always burn and shine in the holy tent, we do well to compare the enlightenment that comes through Christ, which never fails in its power to shine into the mind of believers and to kindle it, or in other words to fill it. For the number seven in a way suggests completeness everywhere, as when it says, for instance, ‘The barren woman has borne seven’ (1 Samuel 2:5), that is, very many, as many as were needed to be enough. Aaron lights the lamps, and so do the rest, the priests who came after him. For the enlightenment from Christ is kept, as it were, unquenched in the churches through the uprightness of those to whom the priesthood has fallen, who make the minds of believers bright by their sound teaching of the mysteries. This, I think, is what is meant by lighting the lamps from evening until morning. anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of Cyril De adoratione Book 9 exists. Translated fresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the earlier English of this book was not used as a base.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

Boundary: §28 opens with the rest of the sentence begun at the end of §27 ('Τύπος | δ' ἂν εἴη καὶ τοῦδε Χριστός'); English 'This too would be a figure | of Christ.' LXX renumbering: Psalm 89:17 LXX = Psalm 90:17 English ('καὶ ἔσται/ἔστω ἡ λαμπρότης κυρίου τοῦ θεοῦ ἡμῶν ἐφ' ἡμᾶς'; Cyril has ἔσται, the LXX ἔστω); Psalm 67:12 LXX = Psalm 68:11 English ('κύριος δώσει ῥῆμα τοῖς εὐαγγελιζομένοις δυνάμει πολλῇ'). 'Beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news of good things' follows the wording of Romans 10:15 (τῶν εὐαγγελιζομένων τὰ ἀγαθά), itself from Isaiah 52:7; cited to Romans. 'Στεῖρα ἔτεκεν ἑπτά' = 1 Samuel 2:5 (1 Kingdoms 2:5 LXX). The seven lamps are not named in Exodus 27:20–21; cited to Exodus 25:37, where the seven lamps of the lampstand are commanded. Uncited possible allusions: the apostles as 'pillars' (Galatians 2:9) and the word resounding through the inhabited world (Psalm 19:4 / Romans 10:18); neither is clear enough to cite. 'ὁ περὶ γῆν αὐτῷ πεποίηται λόγος' rendered 'the word he has spread over the earth'. Exodus 27:20 LXX ἄτρυγον = 'free of dregs' (without lees). 'τὸ καταπέτασμα τὸ ἐπὶ τῆς διαθήκης' = 'the veil that is over the covenant', as in the LXX (the covenant meaning the ark). 'ἐπιείκειαι' (equity, decency) rendered 'uprightness'. 'ἐπὶ ταῖς αὐλαῖς' (about the courts) rendered 'about the court', since the court hangings are what precedes. The section ends mid-phrase ('τὰ τῶν | ἀνοσίων αἱρετικῶν ... μυθάρια'); the English ends '...namely the' and §29 continues 'unholy heretics' ...'.
